coordinates.locator: NOvA seasonal multiple-muon paper, detector description
coordinates.note: The NOvA collaboration quotes the far detector position only to 0.1 degree; precision_m is set to 8 km accordingly. The NOvA official page confirms "The Far Detector is located in Ash River, Minnesota."
coordinates.quote: located on the surface in Minnesota near the U.S.-Canada Border at (48.4°N,92.8°W)

depth_mwe.note: Conflict: the 2020 NOvA multimessenger paper says "a modest 3 meter water-equivalent overburden provided by 1.3 m of concrete and 16 cm of barite"; the 3.6 m.w.e. figure of the 2021 and 2025 papers is used.
depth_mwe.quote: Shielded only by a 3.6 m water equivalent overburden, the FD is exposed to a cosmic-ray flux of 150 kHz.

name: Ash River NOvA far detector laboratory
notes: facility_id is null: the Ash River laboratory is not part of Fermilab and no separate facility record was created in this wave.

Coordinates are coarse. The only coordinate found in a collaboration publication is "(48.4°N, 92.8°W)". Secondary compilations give 48.37917°N, 92.83361°W; that value is not recorded because it has no rank<=7 or collaboration source.

summary.plain: A large surface building in the forest near Ash River, Minnesota, close to the Canadian border. It holds the NOvA far detector, 810 kilometres from the neutrino beam at Fermilab, with only a thin layer of concrete and heavy mineral above it.
summary.technical: Surface (slightly below grade) laboratory near Ash River, Minnesota, 810 km from the NuMI target and 14.6 mrad off the beam axis, housing the 14 kt NOvA far detector under a 3.6 m water-equivalent overburden.
